attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, given as his own description.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps the firm 'unsafe and unreliable' wording and the hedged 'appears to have' wording for the braking problem. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'unsafe and unreliable' as material safety and reliability problems is an ordinary, fair reading, and so is tying 'currently' to July 2023. The result still depends on that reading, because the speaker set no threshold.

evidence.note: Dated July 24, 2023, specialist report on FSD Beta 11.4.6. It says an update targets unnecessary slowdowns that users call phantom braking. This backs the braking part only.
February 2023 recall filing about FSD Beta maneuvers. It is outside the target period and records Tesla disagreeing. It shows earlier defects, not the state of the software in July.
Tesla remedy bulletin from April 2023 (company disclosure). It shows the February recall was addressed before July. It neither proves nor rules out problems in July.
July 26, 2023 report. Musk says 11.4.6 'reduces unnecessary slowdowns', which implies slowdowns existed, and one user's early impressions were positive. This is anecdotal and does not settle safety.

reviews.rationale: The hedged braking part has some contemporary backing: e1 and e4 point to a known problem with unnecessary slowdowns in July 2023. But the packet has no July 2023 evidence for the firm, central claim that FSD Beta was unsafe and unreliable. The recall evidence is from earlier and was remedied, and nothing contradicts the claim. The evidence does not settle the main proposition.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He relays a reported allegation, labelled as alleged, and the claim is about that report.

semantics.note: It keeps 'allegedly' and 'suggesting' and treats 'based on Elon Musk existing' as rhetoric. It is an observation about reported recruiting terms.

contract.note: It is fairly tested against contemporary reporting of the alleged terms and the mission wording. It does not demand primary offer documents for a claim the speaker himself qualified as alleged.

evidence.note: Semafor, July 14, 2023, citing people familiar with the matter. It reports 1% option offers described as like a $200M signing bonus, at a $20B valuation Musk came up with. That matches the alleged terms and the implied valuation.
TIME, July 12, 2023. It confirms that xAI's launch website gave the mission as understanding the true nature of the universe. It says nothing about the money.

reviews.rationale: Contemporary Semafor reporting attributes to xAI recruiting the 1% option offers, the $200M signing-bonus comparison and the $20B valuation, which Musk came up with. TIME confirms the quoted mission. The packet has no correction or contradicting report. The 'Musk existing' remark is rhetoric and is not scored.
